samples.summary: New CLI cannot log in against a backend that predates this change: the extra `codeVerifier` body field is rejected by the global whitelisting ValidationPipe
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:79` now unconditionally sends `JSON.stringify({ code, codeVerifier })` to `POST /auth/cli/exchange`. Any deployed backend built before this diff has `CliExchangeDto` with only `code`, and `packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72` installs `new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, ... })` globally — an unknown `codeVerifier` property makes that request a 400, not a successful exchange. Combined with the new loopback gate (an older backend also never echoes `state`, so `startCallbackServer` 400s its own callback and the login only ends at the 30s timeout), a freshly published CLI is fully broken against any self-hosted server that has not been upgraded. The docs (`docs/design/cli.md:218`) claim "Both are optional on the wire, so a new CLI still works against a server that predates them", which the `forbidNonWhitelisted` pipe contradicts. Fix belongs on the new CLI code: only send `codeVerifier` where the flow is known to be PKCE-capable, or fall back to a code-only retry on 400.

samples.summary: PKCE enforcement is silently downgradable: any caller can start a CLI flow with no (or a malformed) `code_challenge` and receive a plain-bearer authorization code
samples.evidence: `consumeCode` only enforces the verifier when `entry.codeChallenge` is set (`packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:118`). The only producer of that field is `GitHubAuthGuard`, which uses `boundedToken(req.query?.code_challenge, 43, 128, /^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~]+$/)` (github-auth.guard.ts:60-65) and *silently drops* anything failing those bounds instead of rejecting the request, and stores `undefined` when the parameter is absent. `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` with no `code_challenge` is a reachable, unauthenticated entry point (auth.controller.ts:82) that still mints a redeemable code at `POST /auth/cli/exchange` with the code alone — i.e. the new binding is opt-in from the attacker-influenceable query string. The fix belongs on the new code (reject rather than drop a malformed challenge, and/or require a challenge once the CLI floor allows it). Flagging only that a path reaches the protected operation without passing the new check; whether the compatibility trade-off is acceptable is the security lens's call.

samples.summary: The new DTO length bound short-circuits the store's burn-on-mismatch invariant that the controller spec asserts
samples.evidence: `consumeCode` deletes the code before comparing verifiers so a wrong guess burns it (cli-auth.store.ts:113-124), and `auth.controller.spec.ts:384-395` asserts exactly that with `codeVerifier: 'nope'`. In production that request never reaches the controller: the global `ValidationPipe` (main.ts:65) rejects it against `@Length(43, 128)` with a 400, so the code is left spendable and the spec's invariant does not describe shipped behaviour. Same mismatch makes any legacy client with an out-of-range verifier get 400 instead of the intended 401.

samples.summary: `ctx list` (and `status`) still report "Not logged in" as prose on stdout with exit 0 while its sibling `ctx switch` now emits the envelope
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:45-50` — `ctx list` does `console.log('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` and returns 0, and `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:11` does the same. The diff converts `ctx switch` (ctx.ts:63-79) and `login` to the one-line `errorEnvelope`, and `docs/design/cli.md:1051-1057` now states every emitter builds the envelope through `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`, singling out the session commands. An agent that walks `ctx list` before `ctx switch` still gets an unparseable line on the wrong stream.

samples.summary: `sheets export` still flattens a backend error body to a bare Error, losing `code`, contrary to the invariant §9 now documents
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41-42` reads only `error.message` off the backend body and rethrows `new Error(msg)`, so `outputError` stamps `code: 'ERROR'` and the server's `TYPE_MISMATCH` (etc.) is dropped — while the sibling passthroughs in docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155 and slides.ts:161 were converted to `backendErrorEnvelope`, which preserves `code` and extra context. `docs/design/cli.md:1054-1055` now claims the backend-error passthroughs on content *and export* keep their code.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:79` unconditionally posts `{ code, codeVerifier }` to `/auth/cli/exchange`, and `packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72` installs a global `ValidationPipe` with `whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, which 400s any property absent from the DTO. `codeVerifier` exists on `CliExchangeDto` only because this change added it (`packages/backend/src/auth/auth.dto.ts:13-16`), so a backend deployed before the change rejects the new CLI's exchange request outright. The loopback gate compounds it: `login.ts:241-246` refuses any callback without a matching `state`, and `auth.controller.ts:130-134` only echoes `state` when the backend understands `nonce`, so an unupgraded server produces a 30s timeout before the exchange is even attempted. This directly contradicts the contract the repo documents for these very consumers: `docs/design/cli.md:218-221` claims a new CLI still works against a server that predates the parameters, and `docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:41-45,68-69` lists "new CLI works against an old server" and "login still completes end to end against a backend that ignores both new parameters" as satisfied acceptance criteria. I weighed `already-guarded` (the state gate makes the exchange 400 unreachable against a pre-change server) but rejected it: that guard does not prevent the harm, it merely relocates the failure to a timeout, and the finding already accounts for that path. I weighed `out-of-scope` and rejected it too: the CLI is a separately published artifact aimed at self-hosted backends, making an un-upgraded server precisely the out-of-diff consumer this lens covers, and the violated back-compat invariant is asserted in the repo itself. Only the reviewer's suggested remediation is incomplete (removing `codeVerifier` alone would not restore legacy login because the `state` gate still fails) — that qualifies the fix, not the defect.

verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (guard drops a malformed/absent code_challenge at github-auth.guard.ts:59-66; consumeCode enforces the verifier only when entry.codeChallenge is set at cli-auth.store.ts:115-121), but it is not a blast-radius defect. Grep across the repo shows a single production producer (auth.controller.ts:126 -> createCode) and a single consumer (auth.controller.ts:166 -> consumeCode), and a single caller of createState (github-auth.guard.ts:56); every other reference is a spec file. No second entry point reaches the protected mint/redeem operation, and the only in-repo client was updated in lockstep — packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:45-56 always sends nonce and code_challenge and :79 always sends codeVerifier — so no caller is left on the old contract. The optionality is the explicitly documented back-compat contract (cli-auth.store.ts:104-105, docs/design/rest-api.md:338-342 and 352-360, docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:41-45), not an overlooked hole. Every location the reviewer cites is inside the changed files, and the reviewer concedes the trade-off is the security lens's call; per this rubric, a finding statable without leaving the diff and concerning whether a guard is the right security design belongs to the security lens, not blast-radius. The companion binding shipped in the same change also blunts the path: the CLI rejects any callback whose state does not echo its nonce, including state === null (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:240-246), so a challenge-less flow yields a code bound to the initiator's own account and never enters a victim CLI session.
